{{Short description|American chemist}}
'''Joseph Seth Alper''' (born 1941) is professor emeritus of [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Massachusetts, Boston]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lib.umb.edu/files/uploads/files/UMB_2005.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110105125559/http://www.lib.umb.edu/files/uploads/files/UMB_2005.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 5, 2011 |title=Commencement 2005 |date=2005-06-03 |website=University of Massachusetts, Boston |page=44 |access-date=2018-09-17 }}</ref> He is known for his work analyzing [[genetic discrimination]] and other issues related to [[human genetics]] research.<ref name=jwa/><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1HDdBgAAQBAJ |title=Genetic Information: Acquisition, Access, and Control |last1=Thompson |first1=Alison K. |last2=Chadwick |first2=Ruth F. |date=2007-07-23 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=9780585345864 |pages=32 |language=en}}</ref> He is a founding member of the Genetic Screening Study Group.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=h5OilIDEM94C |title=Rights and Liberties in the Biotech Age: Why We Need a Genetic Bill of Rights |last=McKibben |first=Bill |publisher=Rowman & Littlefield |year=2005 |isbn=9780742543416 |pages=233 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sFIhCi6GIu8C |title=A Genetic and Cultural Odyssey: The Life and Work of L. Luca Cavalli-Sforza |last1=Stone |first1=Linda |last2=Lurquin |first2=Paul F. |date=2005 |publisher=Columbia University Press |isbn=9780231133968 |pages=171 |language=en}}</ref> He received his bachelor's degree from [[Harvard University]] in 1963 and his Ph.D. from [[Yale University]] in 1968.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/1979/11/19/misusing-sociobiology-pbto-the-editors-of/ |title=Misusing Sociobiology  |date=1979-11-19 |work=The Harvard Crimson |access-date=2018-09-17 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=jwa>{{Cite web |url=https://jwa.org/encyclopedia/author/alper-joseph |title=Joseph S. Alper  |website=Jewish Women's Archive |language=en |access-date=2018-09-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Alper |first=Joseph |title=Applications of the Group R4 to Atomic Structure Theory |date=1968 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=Yale University |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=unTlZwEACAAJ}}</ref> He did his postdoc in the laboratory of [[Robert J. Silbey]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1968 to 1970.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://web.mit.edu/robertsilbey/students/postdocs.html |title=Robert J. Silbey: Postdocs |website=web.mit.edu |language=en-us |access-date=2018-09-17}}</ref>
